key_insight: Jointly solving keep/recompute/offload and arena offsets removes fragmentation and peak-coincident lifetimes; a correct, useful tool for fixed training graphs.
killer_doubt: Already published: Checkmate solves rematerialization as an ILP and OLLA solves lifetime plus offsets. Gain over today's planners is likely <20%, and MILP on ~1e4-op graphs takes hours.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. To size the residual gain, run Checkmate/OLLA against the PyTorch caching allocator plus selective checkpointing on five transformer configs, measuring peak memory, step time and solve time. ~$20k of GPU time.
prior_art: Checkmate (MLSys 2020) ILP rematerialization; OLLA (Meta, 2022) ILP array lifetime and location; POET (ICML 2022) remat plus paging; XLA rematerialization pass.

key_insight: Shared prefixes (system prompts, documents) are a large share of KV. Storing them once per pod with longest-prefix routing is real demand reduction, and it is already shipping.
killer_doubt: Prior art ships it. The only remaining gain is the cross-pod duplicate share, and moving KV between pods costs ~0.33 MB/token (70B GQA) of network traffic.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. Replay a multi-tenant chat trace through a cache-aware SGLang router and a Mooncake-style global pool, and report the HBM-GB-hours that cross-pod dedup saves beyond per-pod caching.
prior_art: SGLang RadixAttention and cache-aware router; Mooncake (Kimi, FAST'25) global KV pool; NVIDIA Dynamo KV-aware routing; llm-d prefix-aware scheduling.

key_insight: At 4x DRAM prices, GC CPU is cheaper than idle heap headroom. A cross-runtime live price signal turns existing heap knobs into a fleet-wide market-clearing control.
killer_doubt: GC CPU scales as live/(heap-live), so cutting headroom from 2.0x to 1.5x live doubles GC load (5-10% CPU becomes 10-20%). Freed GB count only if the scheduler repacks them.
decisive_experiment: On a ~200-node Kubernetes testbed running JVM and Go services (DeathStarBench, Renaissance), have an agent drive SoftMaxHeapSize/GOMEMLIMIT from a price signal. Measure reclaimed GB that become extra scheduled pods, against CPU and p99. ~$150k.
prior_art: Go GOMEMLIMIT, JVM SoftMaxHeapSize and the OpenJDK ZGC automatic-heap-sizing proposal, .NET DATAS adaptive heaps. A cross-runtime price signal was not found.

key_insight: Frozen weights need no writes, so read-only via-ROM avoids the write-endurance wall entirely. At 100-200 nm pitch, imprinted decks could cost <$1/GB against $20/GB DRAM, with no EUV.
killer_doubt: On PET, 200 nm overlay across 10 cm needs <1 ppm stability against ~20 ppm/K, a miracle, so assume rigid substrates. 1k x 1k passive arrays need selector on/off >=1e4.
decisive_experiment: On rigid Si or glass, nanoimprint 256x256 via-ROM crossbars at 200 and 100 nm pitch with ALD oxide Schottky selectors. Measure on/off ratio, read margin, via defect rate and row access time. University NIL, ~$400k.
prior_art: Mask/via ROM; Intel/Micron 3D XPoint crossbar-over-CMOS; HP Labs nanoimprint crossbars; hardwired-weight LLM chips (Taalas). Printed or imprinted weight ROM not found.

key_insight: Pages that are pure PRNG output compress to (generator, seed, offset), and counter-based Philox can regenerate them bit-exactly on a fault.
killer_doubt: Little memory qualifies: dropout masks are already seed-regenerated, and PRNG pages are likely <5% of a node. At ~2-5 us per 4 KB userfaultfd fault, restore runs ~1 GB/s/thread.
decisive_experiment: Instrument 20 representative training and simulation jobs and count the peak-resident bytes that are pure PRNG output. Below 5%, stop. ~$20k.
prior_art: Philox counter-based RNG (Salmon et al., SC'11); PyTorch/JAX seed-regenerated dropout; Linux discardable/purgeable memory.

key_insight: Bit-exact reversibility makes activation memory independent of depth. With 80-128 layers at long context it removes the dominant term of the training stash for ~1.3-1.5x compute.
killer_doubt: BDIA-transformer (ICML 2025) already reverses bit-exactly without changing the standard architecture. Still open: parity at LLM pretraining scale, plus ~5-15% throughput lost to deterministic kernels.
decisive_experiment: Pretrain BDIA and baseline 1B-7B decoders on ~50B tokens. Compare loss, measured peak HBM, and throughput with deterministic kernels at 32k-128k context. ~$300-600k of GPU time.
prior_art: BDIA-transformer, Zhang/Lewis/Kleijn ICML 2025 (via search snippet); RevNet (2017); Reformer (2020); MacKay et al. fixed-point exact reversible RNNs (NeurIPS 2018).

key_insight: Rotation turns rare catastrophic flips (sign/MSB, super-weights) into diffuse small noise. QuaRot-style rotated INT4 weights already have this property, which could justify relaxed-refresh weight storage.
killer_doubt: Rotation conserves error energy. At 1% BER an INT4 code gains ~0.85 LSB^2 of noise, 10x quantization noise (0.083 LSB^2), leaving ~2.3 effective bits. Long-lived weights accumulate flips.
decisive_experiment: Inject faults at BER 1e-5 to 1e-2 into rotated (QuaRot) and unrotated INT4 Llama weights and plot perplexity against BER. Then measure the retention BER of unrefreshed DDR5 at 85 C on an FPGA rig. ~$80k.
prior_art: QuaRot/SpinQuant Hadamard rotations; EDEN (MICRO 2019) DNNs on approximate DRAM; Phase B card B4-04 (relaxed refresh for mantissa planes).

key_insight: The activation stash lives <~2 s, so refresh-withheld banks suffice. The phase-B tail model gives raw BER ~1.4e-5 at 1 s, 85 C, far below the 1% budgeted.
killer_doubt: E[err|bit] stays nonzero, so codes shrink toward the midpoint. Controller scramblers already randomize flip direction. Unrefreshed banks lose TRR while hot rows see ~1e6 activations/s against a ~1k hammer threshold.
decisive_experiment: On an FPGA DDR5/HBM tester, measure the raw BER of refresh-withheld banks at 85-95 C over 0.2-2 s under training-like row activations, hammering included. Inject the measured error maps into 4-bit-stash training of a 1B model. ~$150k.
prior_art: ActNN (ICML 2021) 2-bit activation stash; RANA (ISCA 2018) lifetime-aware eDRAM refresh; Flikker (ASPLOS 2011); Intel/AMD DDR data scramblers; Phase B B4-04.

key_insight: Idle warm sandboxes are stranded DRAM. Lazy restore of the working set from NVMe in ~5-10 ms replaces warm pools at modest tail-latency cost.
killer_doubt: Production already does this: Lambda SnapStart and Firecracker snapshots. The saving depends on the idle fraction, and a 5-10 ms restore lands on p99 cold starts.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. Optionally replay the Azure Functions trace with FaaSnap-style restore and report DRAM-GB-hours saved against p99 latency.
prior_art: Firecracker snapshots; REAP (ASPLOS'21); FaaSnap (EuroSys'22); AWS Lambda SnapStart.

key_insight: Client signals (typing, tab focus, think-time history) give seconds of warning before the next turn, enough to bring an idle session's KV back from a cold tier just in time.
killer_doubt: Re-prefilling 32k tokens on a 70B model is ~4.6e15 FLOP, ~10 GPU-seconds. Restoring the 10.7 GB of KV from SSD takes ~1.5 s at 7 GB/s, is cheaper, and ships.
decisive_experiment: Replay a chat trace with real think-time distributions. Compare predicted re-prefill against predicted SSD-tier prefetch (LMCache) on GPU-seconds, HBM-GB-hours and TTFT. ~$50k.
prior_art: CachedAttention/AttentionStore (USENIX ATC'24); Pensieve (EuroSys'25); Mooncake KV tiering; LMCache; vLLM recompute preemption.

key_insight: Hash-consing key-sets so that each document is a shape ID plus packed values removes repeated keys and type tags in JSON-heavy in-memory caches.
killer_doubt: This is the hidden-class (Self maps, V8) technique applied to caches. The 2-3x holds only for small, key-heavy documents; listpack/LZ4 capture much of it. A shape-lookup instruction adds little.
decisive_experiment: Load three public JSON API dumps into Redis and into a shape-shared prototype. Measure bytes per document and p99 GET latency. ~$30k.
prior_art: Self maps and V8 hidden classes; JSON Tiles (SIGMOD 2021); Protobuf/FlatBuffers schema-separated encoding; Redis listpack.

key_insight: Forking copy-on-write from one pre-initialized golden snapshot leaves each instance holding only its dirty pages, so many more sandboxes fit per GB.
killer_doubt: Prior art ships it: Zygote, Catalyzer sfork and SnapStart. The 3-8% private-dirty figure assumes read-mostly runtimes, but JIT and GC writes re-dirty most of the heap within minutes.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. Optionally measure the private-dirty fraction after 1e3 invocations for Python, Node and JVM runtimes forked from a golden snapshot.
prior_art: Android Zygote; Catalyzer (ASPLOS'20) sfork; SEUSS (EuroSys'20); AWS Lambda SnapStart.
